opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll, so the maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a contractor with basic security training per Security DB (note lists Analyst role). Contractors without advanced training max out at read, never admin. Admin requested exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Belinda Fuentes (E039) requested admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and the employee's role is Analyst, so admin is not permitted regardless of employment type. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists full_time (max write for an Analyst), while Security lists contractor with basic security training (max read; contractors never get admin). Given the conflicting records, the more restrictive classification (contractor, basic training) applies, capping access at read. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum of read.
